Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — this module's central citation: paragraph (c)'s "reasonably suggesting" clock-start
  language, the whole argument for why internal escalation has to key on suspicion, not
  confirmation. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.170 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.170)**
  — the fatality-notification requirement in paragraph (b), reused from
  `storage-distribution-and-hemovigilance`, and the filer distinction (collecting facility vs.
  compatibility-testing facility) behind this module's fatality-call drill item. Local verbatim
  copy: `sources/cfr/606.170.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — paragraph (b)(19), named only, behind the "consignee notification or retrieval" trigger
  category. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive. Use
  this when you need the officially citable text for a specific year, rather than eCFR's
  continuously updated current version.

- **[An Update on Field Alert Reports (FAR) and Biological Product Deviation Reports
  (BPDR)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EtLmHnBuNJQ)** (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from
  oEmbed `author_name`) — an FDA presentation on how BPDRs are submitted and what the agency
  expects, the external reporting channel behind 606.171(c). Part of it covers drug-side Field Alert
  Reports, which this course doesn't teach. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Biological Product Deviations](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/biological-product-deviations)**
  — FDA's own CBER page for biological product deviation reporting. Read it to see how the agency
  describes the reporting channel behind 606.171, and to confirm current submission details,
  which can change. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Recalls, Market Withdrawals, & Safety Alerts](https://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts)**
  — FDA's hub for public recall and safety-alert information. Useful for seeing what an outward-facing
  recall looks like on the regulator's side; this module names recalls as a trigger category but
  doesn't teach recall procedure. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.404 — Notification to individuals](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.404)**
  — the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule's individual-notice section. This module names a suspected
  data breach only as a trigger category and defers the rules to the future
  `healthcare-security-and-privacy` course; read this to see that a separate, notification-after-
  breach clock exists. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: Escalation policies for effective incident management](https://www.atlassian.com/incident-management/on-call/escalation-policies)**
  — a practical explainer on written escalation policies and on-call paths, the IT-side version of
  agreeing escalation criteria in daylight. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Google SRE Book: Managing Incidents](https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/)** — a
  well-regarded engineering chapter on clear roles and handoffs during an incident, useful as a
  contrast to this module's point that the decision owner for product safety isn't the incident
  commander. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
